questions.title: Remove Value from Ring
questions.description:
A round-table tool expels the FIRST member holding a given value while keeping the ring closed. The harness builds a closed doubly ring with at least two nodes; the value always exists. Relink: if the head itself holds the value, the new head is the node after it and the last node must point to it; otherwise find the node BEFORE the victim and splice around it, fixing prev pointers in both cases. Return the new head; the harness prints the ring from your returned head, walking forward until it returns to the head. Vectors are banned. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    DNode* ring_delete(DNode* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (ring order). Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the ring values from the new head, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, value exists in the ring
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, value exists in the ring

questions.title: Sorted Ring Insert
questions.description:
A circular thermostat schedule keeps temperatures in a closed ring that starts at its SMALLEST value and ascends around. Insert a new value so the ring stays ascending from the head: if the value is smaller than the head it becomes the new head (insert it between the last node and the head), otherwise walk to the node after which it belongs. Maintain prev pointers as you splice. Return the head = the smallest node after insertion; the harness prints the ring from your returned head. Vectors are banned. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    DNode* ring_insert_sorted(DNode* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n ascending integers (ring order, starting at the smallest). Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the ring values from the returned head, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, the ring starts at its smallest value and ascends
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, the ring starts at its smallest value and ascends

questions.title: Josephus Survivor
questions.description:
The classic Josephus problem on a real ring: n people (values 1..n) stand in a closed ring, counting starts at the head as count 1, and every k-th counted person is removed; counting resumes at the person after the removed one. Eliminate people directly on the ring by relinking (fix the prev pointers too) until one remains, and return that survivor's value. Vectors and other buffers are banned — do not copy the values out. The harness builds the closed ring. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int josephus_survivor(DNode* head, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: the integers 1..n in ring order. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the survivor's value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= k <= 10

questions.title: Close the Ring and Report
questions.description:
A telemetry tool receives an OPEN singly-style chain (the last node's next is NULL) and must convert it into a closed ring, then return a four-value report proving the closure: [number of nodes, value at the head, value at the last node, value at the node the last node now points to]. Walk to the last node counting nodes, set its next to the head (and the head's prev to the last node) to close the ring, then read the report off the ring. Sorting is banned. The harness prints the report space-separated. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<int> make_ring_report(DNode* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (open list order).

Output Format:
One line with the four report values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Circular or Open Check
questions.description:
A maintenance tool must tell a closed ring from a plain list. The harness builds the doubly list and, when the extra input mode is 1, closes it properly (tail->next = head and head->prev = tail); mode 0 leaves it open. Report 1 when walking from the head along next pointers brings you back to the head (i.e. the last node points at the head), else 0. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_ring(DNode* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: mode (0 = open, 1 = closed ring).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the structure is a closed ring, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, mode is 0 or 1

questions.title: Pair Sum from Both Ends
questions.description:
A booking system checks whether two DIFFERENT seats (positions) in an ascending doubly list sum exactly to S. Sweep with two pointers: one starting at the head moving forward, one at the tail moving backward through prev; if the sum is too small advance the front pointer, if too large retreat the back pointer, and stop when they meet. Report 1 when such a pair exists, else 0. Vectors and other buffers are banned. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_pair_sum(DNode* head, int S)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers in ascending order. Line 3: S.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if two distinct positions sum to S, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, the list is ascending

questions.title: Insert into Ring After Value
questions.description:
A round-table seating tool inserts a guest right after the FIRST node holding a given value. The harness builds a closed doubly ring; the anchor value always exists. Relink the ring: the new node's next takes the anchor's next, fix that node's prev back to the new node, then point the anchor's next at the new node and its prev at the anchor. Return the original head (unchanged); the harness prints the ring from the head, walking forward until it returns to the head. Vectors are banned. The program scaffolding (includes, the DNode struct and main) is already set up for you.
